findings.trigger: introduzido-pela-r1. POST /api/v1/auth/revoke with {'refreshToken': '<a token from a grant already signed out, expired, or consumed>'}. No authentication, no live credential.
findings.wrong_outcome: The response reports nothing was revoked (accessTokensRevoked 0), the current grant's session is untouched, and the current grant's DOWNLOAD token is gone - the transfer dies mid-stream with no session-level signal. Repeatable at will. Round 1's fix deleted by user_id alone, which made it the one statement a replay of a dead token still hit; before the fix both UPDATEs were no-ops and the replay was harmless. The same widening let a ChatGPT (grantless) sign-out abort an APK download on the operator's phone while leaving the phone session alive.
findings.location: gateway/app/services/store.py:944-946 (the by-actor DELETE), reached from gateway/app/api/routes/auth.py:362-369 which deliberately ignores inspect_refresh_token's status
findings.evidence: Probe: attacker replay of dead grant-A refresh token -> 200 {'accessTokensRevoked': 0}; grant-B download token -> 401 (destroyed); grant-B session -> 200 (untouched); 5/5 replays destroyed a token. Separate probe: chatgpt sign-out -> 200; mobile session -> 200; mobile download token -> 401.
findings.closure: artifact_download_tokens.grant_id added to the model and to migration 0008 (undeployed, so free); revocation scoped to (user_id, grant_id), with grant_id NULL addressing the grantless browser session's own tokens. tests/integration/test_auth.py::test_a_replayed_dead_refresh_token_cannot_kill_a_live_grants_download and ::test_a_grantless_sign_out_does_not_abort_the_phones_download. Both verified to fail without the scoping.

findings.trigger: introduzido-pela-r1. A future /api/v1 route declares Depends(current_principal) and checks no action; or any route whose dependency callable happens to be named 'guard'.
findings.wrong_outcome: It ships. require_action reaches current_principal through its inner closure, so a recursion looking for the latter cannot tell authorization from authentication: a route readable by any authenticated actor of any scope passes the new gate silently. The name-match half is worse - a route with NO authentication at all is judged guarded because one dependency carries that name - and it matches nothing real, since require_action returns a closure called _dependency.
findings.evidence: Added GET /api/v1/secret-dump with only Depends(current_principal) to the real app and called the gate directly: 'GATE VERDICT: PASS'. Control with no dependency at all: gate caught it. Second probe with a dependency named guard and no authentication: 'GATE VERDICT: PASS'. Confirmed independently by the second-caller lens, which also showed the /api/v1/auth/me exemption was inert.
findings.closure: require_action tags its closure with guarded_action (gateway/app/api/auth.py) and the gate reads that attribute; the name match is gone. The /auth/me exemption is now load-bearing, and tests/integration/test_probes.py::test_every_exemption_is_load_bearing fails if any entry stops mattering.

findings.trigger: introduzido-pela-r1. Range: bytes=00000000000000000001-2 (twenty digits: nineteen zeros and a 1) against a 10-byte artifact.
findings.wrong_outcome: The header is dropped and the endpoint answers the whole representation with 200 instead of two bytes with 206 - for a resumed transfer, the entire file re-sent from byte 0, which is the failure Range support exists to prevent. Silent, because an ignored Range is by design indistinguishable from an unsupported one. RFC 9110 section 14.1.1 is 1*DIGIT, so leading zeros are legal; the round-1 bound counted digits while its comment claimed it was lossless because 2**63-1 is 19 digits.
findings.closure: Bound widened to 255 digits - comfortably under CPython's 4300-digit int() threshold and over any sane padding - and the comment corrected to say the bound is on digit count, not magnitude. tests/integration/test_artifacts.py::test_a_zero_padded_range_is_still_a_range.

findings.trigger: introduzido-pela-r1. Read the rewritten docstring at routes/artifacts.py:47 - 'All five live in tests/integration/test_artifacts.py' - then look for the fifth test where it says it lives.
findings.wrong_outcome: test_signing_out_kills_a_download_token_minted_before_it is in tests/integration/test_auth.py. A reader auditing the five narrowings finds four and concludes the revocation property is unpinned - the exact failure round 1 raised, reintroduced by round 1's remedy for it.
findings.evidence: grep -rn for the test name returns tests/integration/test_auth.py:853; grep -c in test_artifacts.py returns 0. Nothing gates the sentence and the suite is green with it wrong.
findings.closure: Docstring corrected: four live in test_artifacts.py and the fifth is named with its file, plus the reason it lives there (what it tests is what sign-out does).

findings.trigger: introduzido-pela-r1. An operator reads the rewritten migration-0008 paragraph, learns schema_guard is not a boot gate, and follows the pointer to the deferred decision.
findings.wrong_outcome: docs/api/README.md points at docs/issues/011-artifacts-downloads-apk/RESUME.md, which does not exist; the directory is empty and nothing under it is tracked. The one unresolved risk the rewrite deliberately escalated is escalated to nowhere - and the rewrite's whole point was that a claim with no artifact behind it is what round 1 found.
findings.evidence: ls -A of the directory is empty; git ls-files docs/issues/ lists only 001 and 004; git check-ignore returns rc=1 so it is not ignored, just absent.
findings.closure: docs/issues/011-artifacts-downloads-apk/RESUME.md written, with both operator decisions, the four counts for each round, and the risk acceptance.

findings.trigger: introduzido-pela-r1. Read purge_expired_audit_events's rewritten paragraph to decide whether the 90-day window is scoped right.
findings.wrong_outcome: It says 'Most record_event call sites in this module write task rows'. Of 19 call sites: 7 task, 5 auth, 3 issue, 2 conversation, 1 epic, 1 artifact. Task is a 37% plurality, not most - and the next sentence is 'a number nothing checks is a claim that rots', so the paragraph asserts a proportion in the same breath as retiring one.
findings.evidence: Counted the entity argument of every record_event( call site in the module: Counter({'task': 7, 'AUTH_ENTITY_TYPE': 5, 'issue': 3, 'conversation': 2, 'epic': 1, 'artifact': 1}).
findings.closure: Neither a count nor a proportion is quoted now; the load-bearing half - that the auth rows are the subset an unauthenticated caller can drive - is kept, with the two-round history of the sentence recorded in it.

findings.trigger: introduzido-pela-r1. Someone swaps gateway/app/main.py:292 and :293 so check_schema runs before create_all, making the gate real.
findings.wrong_outcome: The new test does not fail, though its docstring contracts 'If someone makes the gate real, this test must fail.' The assertion compares REQUIRED_TABLES against Base.metadata.tables and never reads main.py, so the ordering - the only thing that disarms the guard - is unpinned, and the corrected README paragraph would become silently false in the other direction.
findings.location: tests/unit/test_schema_guard.py:110-116 vs the docstring's contract at :98-107
findings.evidence: Probe ran the real startup both ways: create_all -> check_schema (shipped) startup SUCCEEDS; check_schema -> create_all startup REFUSES, naming 0008_artifacts.sql. The two states are distinguishable in reality and indistinguishable to the test.
findings.closure: The test now also asserts run_sync(Base.metadata.create_all) precedes run_sync(check_schema) in main.startup, matching the calls rather than the names (the comment above them mentions check_schema first, which made a naive index-based assertion fire on correct code).

findings.trigger: aberto-da-r1. An operator upgrades a gateway and skips migration 0008 - or 0006, or 0007, any table-only migration.
findings.wrong_outcome: Four shipped files plus the instruction that keeps regenerating them still tell the operator the service will crash-loop until they run it. It does not: the gateway starts, runs the create_all schema with no indexes, no content_type default and no schema_migrations row, and nothing warns. Round 1's correction reached docs/api/README.md only.
findings.location: scripts/install.sh:20, deploy/README.md:46, scripts/apply_migrations.py:12, gateway/app/db/schema_guard.py:50-52 (added by 9ba4e7b), docs/required-reading.md:64-65
findings.evidence: Booted against a database at 0007: startup SUCCEEDED, indexes on artifacts [], content_type default None, schema_migrations rows []. Plus a failing test listing all four files. docs/installation.md:97-98 and docs/security.md:108 are about FORBIDDEN_COLUMNS (0004), which does fire, and were correctly left alone.
findings.closure: All five corrected to distinguish column migrations (which do fail the boot) from table-only ones (which do not); tests/contract/test_docs_match_the_runtime.py::test_no_shipped_file_still_promises_a_boot_gate_for_a_table_only_migration requires each to carry the qualification rather than banning a phrase, so the statement that is true for REQUIRED_COLUMNS survives.

findings.trigger: aberto-da-r1. An integrator reads docs/api/README.md section 'The bytes are not behind the session token' - the document docs/required-reading.md points them at.
findings.wrong_outcome: It still says 'Four things narrow the credential' and enumerates refusals as absent, unknown, expired, wrong-artifact or disabled-account - omitting narrowed and revoked - while routes/artifacts.py now says five and the OpenAPI artifactDownloadToken scheme added by the same fix states that /auth/revoke does kill it. Two documents in one delivery disagree about the security property round 1 was fixed to add, and README is the one written for clients.
findings.evidence: git diff --cached -- docs/api/README.md touches only three other sections; sed of 1060-1082 still shows the four-item list. No test compares the two lists.
findings.closure: README list rewritten to five, each naming its test, with the grant-scoping reason and the '401 here means mint a new token, not refresh the session' rule that the contract now states in two machine-readable places.

findings.trigger: aberto-da-r1. An operator reads .env.example to decide whether to set CODEX_BRIDGE_ARTIFACTS_ROOT.
findings.wrong_outcome: It says the unset default is <checkout>/data/artifacts - a fixed, knowable location - so they leave it unset and place bytes there. The default resolves against the process working directory at import; under the systemd unit that is /opt/codex-bridge/data/artifacts. config.py was rewritten by the round-1 fixes to say exactly this, docs/security.md repeats it, and a test was added to prove it - while the one file an operator actually copies kept the false version.
findings.evidence: cd /tmp/cwdprobe && python -c 'print(settings.artifacts_root)' -> /tmp/cwdprobe/data/artifacts. Found independently by the claim-auditor lens.

findings.trigger: pre-existente. An operator follows docs/installation.md step 4 to build /etc/codex-bridge/env from .env.example.
findings.wrong_outcome: Step 4 enumerates the variables that must be set and never mentions CODEX_BRIDGE_ARTIFACTS_ROOT, while docs/security.md calls it mandatory for a deployment. .env.example ships the line commented out, so the root ends up unset and follows WorkingDirectory=/opt/codex-bridge while the operator script that writes artifacts writes wherever it was run from - and every download then answers a typed 404 that names no path. docs/operations.md has no entry for the surface at all.
findings.evidence: Failing test asserting docs/installation.md names the setting; grep for 'artifact' in docs/operations.md returns nothing.
findings.closure: docs/installation.md step 4 now names it with the consequence of leaving it unset; docs/operations.md gained a 'Download de artefato responde 404 para tudo' symptom entry naming the artifact_content_unavailable log line and its two reasons; tests/contract/test_docs_match_the_runtime.py::test_the_installation_guide_names_every_setting_security_md_calls_mandatory.

questions: nginx location /api/ still sets no proxy_buffering off / proxy_max_temp_file_size, and the download now streams tens of megabytes through it. Carried from round 1, still not measured: no nginx instance available. Worth an operator measurement on frida before the first real APK.

deploy/incus/codexbridge_edge_proxy.py:49 buffers a whole response in memory with a 60s total timeout. Marked RETIRED and out of the request path; if ever reinstated, a large download becomes a timeout and a memory spike.

POST /api/v1/auth/revoke fails OPEN when the audit write fails: the endpoint returns 500 and nothing is revoked - session, refresh chain and download tokens all survive. Pre-existing shape (the two UPDATEs already had it) and unchanged by the fix, which simply joined the same transaction. Whether a sign-out should be fail-closed on an audit failure is a decision, not a tidy-up.

Log volume from artifact_content_unavailable is bounded by the rate limiter at ~120 warnings/min/IP from an authenticated actor against one broken artifact. not reproduced: no unbounded or cheap-unauthenticated log-volume path found. Worth asking whether that is inside the deployment's log budget.

docs/codemap.md claims a symbol count that nothing verifies - the same species of claim as the 'eleven' retired in finding 6 - but it is the generator's own output, not a hand-written assertion. Left alone.
